newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Romania is technically prepared to start the election process, head of government's secretariat for preparing November 3 polls, Adrian Duta, told a news conference.
* Romania and Ukraine will resume treaty talks in January 1997 and will hold a summit meeting in the first half of next year, foreign ministry spokesman Sorin Ducaru said.

* Finance ministry state secretary Gheorghe Oana denied rumours that domestic fuel prices would go up to $1.0 per litre in the first term of 1997, saying a 15 percent rise in fuel prices was expected.
* Central Electoral Bureau decided that ballots to elect Romania's president on November 3 should be reprinted in southern Calarasi county where name boxes did not feature candidates' electoral sign.
* National Liberal Alliance presidential candidate Nicolae Manolescu is campaigning at the Nuclear Physics Institute nearby Bucharest.
* Greater Romania Party's Vadim Tudor will hold electoral rally in the eastern town of Vaslui this afternoon.
* Gheorghe Funar, National Unity Party's presidential candidate, is visiting the Transylvanian county of Harghita.

* Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu to attend Central European Initiative's conference in Graz, Austria, starting November 8. The meeting will dicuss ways to boost regional countries' chances of EU integration.
* Romanian army Chief of Staff General Dumitru Cioflina met his Yugoslav counterpart in Belgrade to discuss bilateral military cooperation agreement.

* South Korea still leads foreign investors in Romania with Daewoo Heavy Industries putting more than $200 million in various industrial projects, with Italy and Germany following, Romania's Chamber of Commerce said. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
